answer: A reputation bond makes Sybil attacks costly: every agent must lock a refundable stake before joining the market, and the stake is slashed when peers flag fake identities. Like climbers sharing one summit, honest agents protect the shared peak because cheating burns their own deposit. One attacker facing a dune of identical-looking clones still has to fund each one, so the cost scales linearly, while detection only needs one mirror: a duplicate-behavior check that exposes copycat agents and confiscates their bonds before they can drain the economy.
